baseline_kernel: FlashMLA SM100 V32 flash_fwd_splitkv_mla_fp8_sparse_kernel plus flash_fwd_mla_combine_kernel

bottleneck.evidence: Serving-native Nsight Compute on the exact explicit flashmla_kv ABI shows one shared-memory-heavy CTA per SM, very few eligible warps, long-scoreboard and barrier stalls, and substantial excessive shared-memory wavefronts/bank conflicts; Nsight Systems shows the fused main kernel dominates or matches the separate combine cost.

approaches.summary: Preserved the fixed metadata envelope but reduced useful split partitions separately for the two production buckets to lower combine partial-output traffic.
approaches.why: Combine traffic and duration fell, but reduced split parallelism slowed the dominant main kernel and every repeated eager paired series regressed in both buckets.

approaches.summary: Built an isolated FlashMLA binary that staged each dequant group's four rows together with padding intended to rotate shared-memory banks.
approaches.why: The padded group stride violated the SM100 gather4 TMA destination alignment contract and faulted before output; an aligned pad exceeds the shared-memory cap while zero padding removes the intended rotation.

lesson: For one-wave FlashMLA sparse decode, fewer split partitions can reduce combine bytes yet still lose because main-kernel parallelism is more valuable.  Any bank-rotation layout for bulk tensor gather must satisfy the instruction's shared-address alignment and the full dynamic-shared-memory budget before GPU testing; source-level logical mapping and compilation are not enough.
